# Set up
1. Load the tidyverse library. 
```{r}
library(tidyverse) 
```

2. Load the billboard data. 
```{r}
data("billboard")
```

3. Describe the dataset. 
**The dataset shows the rankings for a song in the Billboard top 100 and for which ranking it was as for each week in week 1-76 period.** 

4. Print the column names from this dataset. 
```{r}
colnames(billboard)
```

5. Print the first 5 entries in the dataset. 
```{r}
billboard[1:5,]
```


# Practice
1. Create a subset of data that has Jay-Z as the only artist. How many songs are in it?
```{r}
billboard %>% filter(artist == "Jay-Z")
```
**There are 5 songs Jay-Z made that ended up in the filter.**

2. In the original dataset, use filter to find information about the song "All the small things." What was the highest position (i.e. lowest number) this song reached on the billboard 100? 
```{r}
billboard %>% filter(track == "All The Small Things")
```
**The highest position it reached was in week 12, where it ended up at number 6 on the Top 100.**

3. Create a subset of data for songs Tim McGraw sang. Summarize the data for wk 1.
```{r}
billboard %>% filter(artist == "McGraw, Tim")
McGrawTim <- billboard %>% filter(artist == "McGraw, Tim")
summary(McGrawTim$wk1)
```

4. Create a function that can be used to determine if Britney Spears sang the song. 

```{r}
britneySpears <- function(arg1){
  ifelse(billboard$artist=="Spears, Britney", "yes", "no")
}
```

5. Test your function on the billboard data. Save the results to a new column called "wasItBritney"
```{r}
billboard$wasItBritney <- britneySpears(billboard$track)
print(billboard$wasItBritney)
```
6. Use a for loop to determine if a song placed 50 or below or placed above 50 during the first week. 
```{r}
billboard$forBillboard <- NA

for(i in 1:nrow(billboard)){
  billboard$forBillboard[i] <- billboard$wk1[i]<50
}
```
7. Use an if else statement to determine the same information as you obtained with the for loop. 
```{r}
billboard$ifElseBillboard <- NA

for(i in 1:nrow(billboard)){
  if(billboard$wk1[i]<50){
    billboard$ifElseBillboard[i] <- "yes"
  }
  else{billboard$ifElseBillboard[i]<- "no"}
}
```
8. Compare your results in 6 and 7. 
```{r}
print(billboard$forBillboard)
print(billboard$ifElseBillboard)

```

**Both of them got the same results. I was able to change the words in the columns for my if else statements, but the for loop got the same results with less. For loops used TRUE/FALSE by default.**
